messages.author: 8ae1efaa2cf53fab
messages.subject: 6.0 - test versus reference.
parts:
Hello all,

I have 15 patient samples and 28 'controls' (6.0 chips). I would like
to identify CNRs by comparing the 15 patients to a reference generated
from the 28 controls. Is this possible? The vignette seems to
indicate that the options available are either:
- case-control pairs of samples
- samples relative to a common reference, where the common reference
is by default calculated as the robust average across samples, i.e.
the 15 patient samples?

cheers

Lavinia.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] 6.0 - test versus reference.
parts:
Hi Lavina,

first, install the latest patch:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Then, let 'cesN' be the CnChipEffectSet that holds all arrays in your
data set, and assume for simplicity than arrays 1:15 are the "samples"
and arrays 16:43 are the "normals". Then you can do:

# Extract the normal
cesR <- extract(cesN, 16:43);

# Calculate the (robust) average of these 28 arrays
ceR <- getAverageFile(cesR);
print(ceR);

# Use this robust average as the reference for all 43 arrays
sm <- CbsModel(cesN, ceR);
print(sm);

# Fit the model on array 1...
fit(sm, arrays=1, chromosomes=19, verbose=log);

Above I put all 43 arrays in the setup of the segmentation model; then
you can run the segmentation on a few of your normals as well to
verify that the normals are "normal".

Let me know if there are any problems

Cheers

Henrik

Hi,

sorry about that, I forgot to include another patch that fixes a bug
causing getChipType(..., fullname=FALSE) for AffymetrixCelFile:s to
ignore argument 'fullname'. Retry after doing:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Hope it helps

/Henrik
